fieldMarks: Male: gray with a white-edged black throat and chest, red combs above the eyes and a black tail tipped rusty (except the Franklin's form).
Female: reddish or grayish with a shorter, darker tail than the ruffed grouse and black-and-white barring on the belly.
behavior: Notoriously tame and easy to overlook.
Males give a very low krrrk and drum with the wings.
Feeds on the ground in summer and almost entirely in trees in winter, eating conifer needles.
Mostly permanent resident; some females walk short distances between seasonal territories.
habitat: Dense conifer forest of spruce, pine, fir or hemlock with undergrowth; also regenerating jack pine burns.
range: Across Alaska and the boreal forest of Canada, south into the Rockies, Great Lakes states and northern New England.

lookalikes.name: Ruffed grouse
lookalikes.howToTell: Ruffed grouse have a longer tail, longer broader side bars and lack belly barring.
